tx.t: This week we are studying the life of Marie Curie, one of the most important scientists of the twentieth century. She was born in Warsaw in eighteen sixty-seven and moved to Paris to study when she was twenty-four.

Together with her husband Pierre, she discovered two new elements, polonium and radium, in eighteen ninety-eight. In nineteen oh three she won the Nobel Prize in Physics, becoming the first woman ever to win a Nobel Prize.
In nineteen eleven she won a second Nobel Prize, this time in Chemistry. During the First World War, she developed mobile X-ray units that doctors used to treat wounded soldiers.
She died in nineteen thirty-four, probably because of her long exposure to radiation.

tx.t: In this lecture I will describe the world's rainforests and why scientists want to protect them. Rainforests cover only about six per cent of the Earth's land surface.
However, they are home to more than half of all the plant and animal species on land. The Amazon is the largest rainforest, and it spreads across nine countries.
A rainforest has four main layers: the emergent layer, the canopy, the understorey and the forest floor. Most animals live in the canopy, where there is plenty of light and fruit.
Many modern medicines come from rainforest plants, and scientists believe thousands more are still unknown.

Use grew quickly. Within three years the number of journeys had risen by forty-five per cent, and on a busy day there were more than three thousand trips.

Today, a ride costs two pounds fifty-five for the first half hour, and the first fifteen minutes are free for residents.

tx.t: Let us begin with the early history of the bicycle. The first machine of this kind was built in eighteen seventeen by a German baron called Karl von Drais, and it had no pedals.

In the eighteen sixties, pedals were fixed to the front wheel, and the machines were nicknamed boneshakers because of their hard wheels. In the eighteen seventies, the penny-farthing had a huge front wheel, which made it fast but dangerous.

The safety bicycle of the eighteen eighties had two wheels of the same size and a chain driving the back wheel. In eighteen eighty-eight, John Dunlop introduced the air-filled tyre, which made riding far more comfortable.

items.title: Ulugh Beg and the Samarkand Observatory

tx.t: Today I would like to tell you about Ulugh Beg, the ruler and astronomer of Samarkand. Ulugh Beg was a grandson of the conqueror Timur, and he ruled Samarkand in the first half of the fifteenth century.
He built a great observatory in Samarkand in the fourteen twenties. Its main instrument was a giant sextant, with a radius of about forty metres.
With it, his team made a catalogue of more than a thousand stars that was used for centuries. His measurement of the length of the year was wrong by less than a minute.

tx.t: This lecture is about a successful conservation project in Fenwick Marsh. In nineteen eighty-four, only thirty-two pairs of red squirrels were counted there.
The main reason for the decline was the loss of hedges and woodland. So volunteers and rangers planted new woodland and hedges.
By twenty fourteen, the number had risen to two hundred and seventy-one pairs, which shows that careful management can work.
